blocks.text: Step 1: Recognize the friction in presentation work
Identify where the format slows you down: blank-slide paralysis, dense information, competing visual choices, or pressure to persuade quickly.

blocks.alt: The challenges of creating slide presentations

blocks.text: Step 2: Separate the message from the design burden
Define the core idea first. Let Gemini accelerate layout, formatting, and visual production while you retain control of the story.

blocks.alt: The visual canvas and its presentation challenges

blocks.text: Step 3: Map each friction point to a Gemini workflow
Use Gemini to create or edit slides, generate visuals, draft speaker notes, summarize decks, and answer questions about the content.

blocks.alt: Gemini in Google Slides course workflows

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.
Before designing slides, help me define the audience, the one-sentence outcome, the three-part narrative, and the evidence required for a presentation about [topic].

lessons.title: Why Do Slide Presentations Need AI?

blocks.text: Step 1: Open Google Slides with Gemini available
Open a new or existing presentation and confirm your account has Gemini access. Use Gemini as your design and storytelling partner.

blocks.alt: Introduction to Gemini in Google Slides

blocks.text: Step 2: Choose the right Gemini interface
Use Ask Gemini for broad requests, Enhance this slide for layouts, and Help me visualize for slides, images, or infographics.

blocks.alt: Ways to interact with Gemini in Slides

blocks.text: Step 3: Configure Workspace Intelligence and sources
In the prompt box, add relevant Drive, Gmail, Chat, or web sources, then review every result for accuracy and sensitive information.

blocks.alt: Workspace Intelligence and Gemini source settings

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.
Using @[Drive file], create a five-slide presentation for [audience] that explains [topic]. Use only information supported by the source and flag anything that needs verification.
blocks.title: Ready-to-use prompt

lessons.title: Introduction to Gemini in Google Slides

blocks.text: Step 1: Use Creating workflows when starting a deck
Choose Creating when you have a blank canvas, rough notes, or a source document that needs to become a structured presentation.

blocks.alt: Creating workflows in the course

blocks.text: Step 2: Use Enhancing workflows when improving a draft
Choose Enhancing when the deck needs clearer text, better layouts, new visuals, edited images, or stronger speaker notes.

blocks.alt: Enhancing workflows in the course

blocks.text: Step 3: Use Consuming workflows when reviewing or taking action
Choose Consuming to understand a dense deck, validate it against sources, or transform it into an email, report, or video.

blocks.alt: Consuming workflows in the course

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Use this rule to choose the right Gemini workflow.
Blank or notes → Creating; existing draft → Enhancing; completed or unfamiliar deck → Consuming.
blocks.title: Decision rule

lessons.title: How to Navigate the Rest of This Course

blocks.text: Step 1: Strategize the presentation with Ask Gemini
Define the audience, objective, narrative, number of slides, and desired tone before asking Gemini to generate content.

blocks.alt: Strategize a presentation with Ask Gemini

blocks.text: Step 2: Generate a presentation using trusted sources
Choose Add sources, attach the relevant Drive files, and ask Gemini to create a presentation plan grounded in those sources.

blocks.alt: Generate a presentation and add sources

blocks.text: Step 3: Review the plan and add slides that match the deck
Review the structure before generation. Ask Gemini to use the existing deck as style context when adding another slide.

blocks.alt: Add a new slide that matches the existing style

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Create a [number]-slide presentation for [audience] about [topic], grounded in @[source]. Structure it as problem, evidence, recommendation, and next steps. Keep titles concise and match the current deck's visual style.
blocks.title: Ready-to-use prompt

blocks.text: Step 1: Improve an existing slide layout
Select a slide and use Enhance this slide to generate a cleaner layout. Compare the preview before replacing or inserting it.

blocks.alt: Enhance an existing slide

blocks.text: Step 2: Create a custom visual or infographic
Open Help me visualize and describe the information, style, aspect ratio, and audience. Use an infographic for processes or data stories.

blocks.alt: Generate a custom infographic

blocks.text: Step 3: Refine the script and speaker notes
Ask Gemini to shorten crowded slide text, then create speaker notes that add context without repeating the slide word for word.

blocks.alt: Insert speaker notes with Gemini

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Enhance this slide for [audience]. Keep one clear message, reduce the on-slide copy to three concise points, suggest one useful visual, and write 60 seconds of speaker notes that explain the evidence.

lessons.title: Enhancing: Refining Text and Visuals in Your Slides

blocks.text: Step 1: Summarize the presentation
Ask Gemini for a concise summary of the deck's purpose, key claims, decisions, risks, and unresolved questions.

blocks.alt: Summarize a presentation with Gemini

blocks.text: Step 2: Ask targeted questions and validate the answers
Ask about dates, owners, metrics, or recommendations. Compare Gemini's answer with the original source before relying on it.

blocks.alt: Validate a presentation against a source

blocks.text: Step 3: Turn the deck into a follow-up action
Use the presentation context to draft a follow-up email, create a report in Docs, or convert the material into Google Vids.

blocks.alt: Draft a follow-up email from the deck

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Summarize this presentation in five bullets, list every decision and action item with an owner and deadline, identify claims that require source verification, and draft a follow-up email for the attendees.
blocks.title: Ready-to-use prompt

blocks.text: Step 1: Focus on the story and outsource repetitive design work
Keep ownership of the message and audience outcome. Let Gemini accelerate layouts, formatting, imagery, and first-draft text.

blocks.alt: The two core principles for using Gemini in Slides

blocks.text: Step 2: Treat Gemini as a collaborative editor
Ask Gemini to critique, shorten, reorganize, or regenerate the content while preserving the facts and your intent.

blocks.alt: Use Gemini as a collaborative editor

blocks.text: Step 3: Apply the workflow to the next real presentation
Choose a real deck and repeat the full cycle: create, enhance, consume, verify, and present.

blocks.alt: Apply Gemini skills to the next workflow

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Review this deck as a critical presentation coach. Identify the weakest part of the narrative, the three most crowded slides, unsupported claims, and the single revision that would most improve audience understanding.

blocks.text: Step 1: Create an introductory slide with Ask Gemini
Ask Gemini to create an introductory slide for the presentation's topic, audience, and objective.

blocks.alt: Open Ask Gemini and create an introductory slide

blocks.text: Step 2: Reference a Drive document to create a summary slide
Use @ to select a Drive file, ask Gemini for a summary slide, preview the result, and select Insert.

blocks.alt: Reference a Drive document and create a summary slide

blocks.text: Step 3: Generate and insert a custom image
Describe the subject, setting, composition, and style, then insert the generated image that best supports the message.

blocks.alt: Generate and insert a custom image

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.
Create an introductory slide for [topic] aimed at [audience]. Then use @[Drive file] to create a summary slide. Finally, generate a [style] image of [subject] that supports the main recommendation.

blocks.text: Step 1: Open or copy the sample deck
Open the presentation. Make a copy if you need to preserve the original, then confirm the Gemini side panel is available.

blocks.alt: Open the sample Google Slides deck

blocks.text: Step 2: Summarize the presentation's purpose and key points
Ask for a concise summary covering the deck's purpose, themes, evidence, decisions, and open questions.

blocks.alt: Generate a presentation summary

blocks.text: Step 3: Draft a follow-up email
Keep the presentation context active and ask Gemini for an email with the summary, action items, owners, deadlines, and next steps.

blocks.alt: Draft a follow-up email with action items

Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Summarize this deck for someone who missed the meeting. State its purpose, five key points, all decisions, unresolved questions, and action items. Then draft a concise follow-up email with owners and next steps.

blocks.text: Step 1: Research the presentation topic
Tell Gemini the topic, audience, goal, and constraints. Explore key concepts, examples, opposing viewpoints, and credible evidence.

blocks.alt: Research a presentation topic with Gemini

blocks.text: Step 2: Create a structured outline and export it to Docs
Ask Gemini for sections with timing, supporting points, examples, and transitions, then export the outline to Google Docs.

blocks.alt: Export a structured presentation outline to Docs

blocks.text: Step 3: Generate talking points in Google Docs
Ask Gemini in Docs for detailed talking points. Specify the section, tone, audience, and speaking time, then edit for accuracy.

blocks.alt: Create detailed talking points in Google Docs

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Research [topic] for a [duration]-minute presentation to [audience]. Build a timed outline with a hook, three sections, evidence, transitions, and a closing action. Then write natural talking points that do not simply repeat the slides.
blocks.title: Ready-to-use prompt

blocks.text: Step 1: Select the content to visualize
Open a slide with text or data that needs stronger visual treatment. For a cover design, create a blank slide.

blocks.alt: Open slide content or a blank cover slide

blocks.text: Step 2: Choose a visualization mode and enter a prompt
Open Help Me Visualize, select Infographic or Slide, and describe the message, hierarchy, audience, and visual style.

blocks.alt: Choose Infographic or Slide mode and enter a prompt

blocks.text: Step 3: Review and insert the generated design
Check the result for factual accuracy, legibility, and visual hierarchy, then insert the selected design into the deck.

blocks.alt: Insert the generated presentation design

blocks.text: Step 4: Takeaway
Copy this prompt and adapt it to your presentation.

Create an infographic based on this slide for [audience]. Preserve every verified fact, establish a clear reading order, use concise labels, and apply a clean [style] visual system with accessible contrast.
